question.text: Under most Indian DTAAs, dividend income is taxable in the source country in the hands of which party, and at what range of withholding rates on gross dividends?

answer.text: Any entity receiving the dividend, at 20% to 30% of gross dividends
The country offering the lower tax rate, at 0% of gross dividends
The beneficial owner of shares, at 5% to 15% of gross dividends
Only individual shareholders, at 10% to 20% of gross dividends

explanation.text: The Logic: Under most Indian DTAAs, dividend is taxable in the source country in the hands of the beneficial owner of shares at a rate ranging from 5% to 15% of the gross amount of the dividends. The Trap: Treaty benefits are not available to any recipient of dividend income -- they are available only when the recipient is the beneficial owner of the shares paying the dividend. Note: Stick to the workbook scope: source-country DTAA rate (5% to 15%) applies to the beneficial owner of the shares. Wider concepts such as conduit entities, treaty shopping, economic substance, and GAAR are not covered in this rule on page 228.
